qualification: local A05.3 single-access memory-target chaining measurement; not A05.3 closure, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.boundary: Direct-chain and IBTC targets may carry one memory callback when the active execution supplies memory capabilities. The callback authority spans the complete native chain and A05.4 recovery resolves a failed callback against any resident target.
candidate.conservativeExclusions: Targets requiring restartable multi-access reads remain dispatcher-separated because that policy is currently selected for the entry block. Baseline targets with interpreter guards also remain excluded.
candidate.regressionCoverage: A callback-free source chains directly into a memory-bearing target in both baseline and tier-one modes. A forced target read fault restores the exact two-block prefix and returns through one native dispatcher entry.

verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,553 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the frozen fixture was executed explicitly.
verification.diffCheck: git diff --check passed before the focused implementation commit.

disposition.reason: Single-access callback targets more than doubled generated bypasses and reduced normalized dispatcher entries by about one third, but the within-run reduction remains far below the strict greater-than-95-percent gate and wall time regressed. The card stays open.

limitations: This is one local measurement, sufficient to reject gate closure but not to make a stable wall-time comparison.
Retired instruction totals differ from the reference run, so normalized and within-run dispatcher ratios are reported instead of an unmatched raw-count claim.
Multi-access restartable-read targets and guarded baseline targets remain dispatcher-separated.
